analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (4495–5336) and the supplied change map/partial patch. The visible changed BASE text at 4860–4864 and 4870 describes Gemma prompt expert reductions and separates numerical equality from throughput qualification. Replacement HEAD text at 4901–4917 and 4922–4927 is not supplied, so its security implications cannot be established here. The patch also announces an exception to singleton defaults for serial-prefill Gemma pipelines, including coordinator-installed sessions; the referenced new lane-policy section and implementing code are outside these units.
Surrounding contracts cover artifact/manifest pinning, rank agreement, request-owned KV and recurrent state, encrypted residual/media transfer, per-lane memory charging, cancellation and release fences, authenticated prefix partitions, media ingress lifetime, serving grants and READY capability checks. These are relevant to A-001, A-018, T-007/T-027, T-008, T-010, T-028, T-041 and TB-011; the supplied BASE text is context, not evidence that the PR implements or weakens those controls. In particular, existing TP memory/SSD prefix tiers (5004–5007) must not be reported as newly introduced or equated with the standalone production tier described by T-041.
No concrete regression is independently supported by these documentation-only BASE units. Integration should examine the new Gemma lane default and revised arithmetic policy against the changed implementation: width propagation into LOAD agreement and admission quotes, request isolation, cancellation/retirement fences, cache/arithmetic namespace separation, and qualification/serving-grant restrictions. Missing HEAD sections and implementation leave these PR-specific conclusions unresolved; no billing, authorization, attestation or encryption bypass is established here.
